name: dots.mocr

lineage.how_derived: successor with SVG/graphics parsing added; the paper is arXiv 2603.13032

purpose: Multilingual document parsing that also converts structured graphics (charts, UI layouts, scientific figures) into SVG code; grounding, recognition and dialogue (card).

license.name: MIT (card tag) plus dots.mocr LICENSE AGREEMENT (custom, MIT prevails on conflict)
license.notes: Agreement text read; same terms as dots.ocr: commercial use and redistribution granted, but 3.3 prohibits extracting sensitive personal data without legal basis and "unauthorized digitization of publications/document scanning", 5.2 prohibits processing GDPR/HIPAA-protected personal data without consent and safeguards; automatic termination on breach.

architecture.kind: vision-language model, 3.04B parameters (safetensors total), dots.ocr architecture with custom code

variants.notes: the rednote-hilab path redirects; size from parameter count x 2 bytes

pc-16gb.notes: BF16 about 6 GB; one model at a time in Tona

engine_support.notes: no llama.cpp or GGUF support confirmed for dots.mocr

benchmarks.name: MDPBench overall (17 languages)
benchmarks.variant: dots.mocr; digital 90.5, photographed 77.2, best open model in the table

benchmarks.name: MDPBench German pages (DE column)
benchmarks.harness: run by the dots.mocr authors (same group as the benchmark)

strengths: highest overall score among open parsers on MDPBench incl. photographed pages
weaknesses: license agreement restricts personal-data and scanned-publication use
3B is larger than the 1B parsers with similar German scores (GLM-OCR 82.7)
best_for: accurate parsing of mixed digital and photographed pages, charts to SVG
soft.maturity: same vendor as dots.ocr; releases March 2026; 58,829 downloads at check time

tona_fit.reason: top quality among open parsers on third-party multilingual/photo tests, fits every class; held back by the personal-data clauses in the license agreement (invoices, ID-bearing scans) and an unconfirmed llama.cpp route, not by missing Tona support
blockers: license clause on personal data and scanned publications
Tona engine has no vision/OCR architecture

sources.note: HF API and README; rednote-hilab/dots.mocr is the card link in the README
leaderboard table in the dataset README

open_questions: GGUF / llama.cpp support for the dots architecture
legal reading of the personal-data clauses for local private use
